newsitem.title: UK: Activists clash with police at London street party.
newsitem.headline: Activists clash with police at London street party.

text.p: Environmental activists commandeered London's Trafalgar Square for a huge party on Saturday which erupted into clashes with police in riot gear.

Police said at least four officers were injured when demonstrators bombarded them with cans, paint, sticks and smoke bombs at the entrance to Prime Minister John Major's official residence in Downing Street early in the day.
Several arrests were made as police donned protective clothing and called in reinforcements on horseback.

The protesters were forced back to Trafalgar Square, north of Downing Street, where the main bulk of the 7,000 marchers had arrived peacefully for a rally highlighting disparities in living standards.
Britain votes in a general election on May 1 with the Conservatives, who have ruled for 18 years, lagging badly behind the opposition Labour party in opinion polls.

During the afternoon and early evening, police were involved in a series of running skirmishes with some of the protesters in the square, unleashing baton charges against a hail of bottles and other ammunition.
A police spokeswoman said protesters broke up paving stones and used the pieces as missiles. One man emerged from the melee with blood pouring from his face.
Only 100 or so protesters, wearing masks and hoods, were involved in the clashes with police, who sealed off the area to prevent any more people from joining the party.
The remainder of the around 1,500 activists partied, waving "Reclaim the Streets" banners and dancing to music blaring from loudspeakers.
Some of them had managed to drape huge banners reading "Trees Not MPs" and "Reclaim Your Environment" above the Canadian High Commission and the National Gallery.

The earlier march, organised by dockers from the north-west port of Liverpool who were sacked in a long-running industrial dispute, had included hundreds of unemployed, disabled people, pensioners and aslyum seekers.
A police spokeswoman said the trouble began when a group of activists harangued police standing behind barriers and then tried to climb the gates leading to Downing Street.

During the evening, police succeeded in driving the crowds out of Trafalgar Square and dispersing them around central London. As they went, the activists smashed shop windows and attacked cars and a bus, which drove away quickly.
Behind them, the square was left littered with beer cans and rubbish. Its trees and shrubs had been trampled and broken.

"Reclaim the Streets", one of several "direct action" groups that have emerged in Britain over the past five years, had warned it planned a "spectacular event" during the march and police had been on alert for trouble.
The group last year succeeded in closing one of the main highways into London and holding a two-day street party on it.
